headline: SemantEq uses proof-term auditing to test equivalence between formal mathematical statements
summary: SemantEq defines a reference-based test for whether two Lean statements can be transformed into one another using constrained, auditable steps, and checks the proof terms that Lean verifies. In the authors’ ProofNetVerif test, their search program reports 100.0% precision under both published and author-adjudicated labels, while recall is 51.4% and 65.6%, respectively, on the 1,303 of 1,452 pairs that elaborated. The authors changed 102 labels from equivalent to non-equivalent. A second proof-audit program reports 330 of 407 equivalent pairs accepted and none of 104 non-equivalent pairs under its best prompt. These are paper-reported results. The method depends on a trusted formal reference and does not test whether that reference matches the original informal statement; independent reproduction and external label review remain open.
